core_obligations: Reduce nonvanishing to a computation in an explicit module: to show that xi_1 X xi_2 - xi_2 X xi_1 is nonzero, display an O-module on which it acts nontrivially (proof lines 2567-2573).

Write down that module: define theta_i = q^{2i} + q^{-2i} for i = 0, 1, 2 and vartheta = (q^4-q^{-4})(q^2-q^{-2})(q-q^{-1})^2, and record the four-dimensional module V with the two displayed matrices for X and Y (proof lines 2574-2600).

Compute one entry: in the matrix representing xi_1 X xi_2 - xi_2 X xi_1 with respect to that basis the (4,3)-entry is -q^2, which is nonzero, so the first commutator is nonzero (proof lines 2601-2606).
Conclude: interchanging the roles of X and Y gives the nonvanishing of the second commutator, and the statement about O cap J follows (proof lines 2607-2611).
proof_roadmap: Produce an explicit four-dimensional module with displayed matrices for X and Y (proof lines 2572-2600).
Compute a single matrix entry of the commutator in that module, and get the second element by symmetry (proof lines 2601-2611).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that two explicit elements of the algebra O, the commutators xi_1 X xi_2 - xi_2 X xi_1 and xi_1 Y xi_2 - xi_2 Y xi_1, are nonzero, and that O cap J is nonzero (statement lines 2554-2564). The proof does not manipulate the algebra: it exhibits a four-dimensional O-module, adapted from a cited tridiagonal-pair construction, in which X and Y are given by two explicit 4x4 matrices built from theta_i = q^{2i}+q^{-2i} and from vartheta (proof lines 2574-2600), and then verifies nonvanishing by computing the single (4,3)-entry -q^2 of the matrix of the first commutator (proof lines 2601-2606). The second element follows by interchanging X and Y. The step that carries the content is the choice of module and the entry computation, since the elements themselves are defined abstractly and the whole point is that they do not vanish; the final sentence closes the O cap J clause. H2.
